symptom: LLM audit judge applies image-enrichment-completeness criterion to hierarchical (non-flat) documents, but classify_verdict at helpers.py:1244 only tracks image_enrichment_ratio for flat docs (content_class flat_prose/flat_mixed via the image_enrichment_promoted gate at line 1274). For hierarchical docs (content_class='' or 'unknown'), classify_verdict is called at client.py:1518 with image_enrichment_ratio=None and content_class='', so unenriched <!-- image --> markers in tree node text are invisible to the code-level gate. The stored verdict correctly returns PASS (502 nodes, depth 4, good max_leaf_ratio), but the LLM audit judge sees 12 unenriched image markers and downgrades to MARGINAL. This is a gate-vs-judge alignment gap, not a code bug in classify_verdict itself.

symptom: RFC-027 D7 dynamic timeout scaling was implemented as dead code: chunked_docling_timeout_s() exists in converters.py but is never imported or called by worker.py. The worker always uses fixed CHILD_TIMEOUT=1770s (29.5min). world-stats-pocketbook-2023.pdf (292 pages, 6.4MB) requires 24-49 min for Docling conversion at 5-10s/page on CPU. With 2 chunks of ~150 pages each, total processing can exceed the fixed 1770s timeout, causing the worker to SIGTERM/SIGKILL the child subprocess before any artifacts are persisted.

symptom: _is_garbled_blob checks PUA (U+E000-U+F8FF) at 3% threshold but has NO check for Arabic Presentation Forms (U+FB50-FDFF, U+FE70-FEFF). These are positional glyph variants that indicate font-encoded garble, but they are valid Unicode points outside PUA range. _infer_script (line 962) counts them as Arabic (lines 971-976), reinforcing the false-negative. Documents with 93%+ presentation forms pass all garble checks and store PASS verdict.

doc: مرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (13) لسنة 2022 بشان التأمين ضد التعطل عن العمل - Copy.pdf
symptom: Run 11 meta.json: verdict PASS/cat_b_promoted, content_class=flat_mixed, flat_char_count=5972, 75 blocks, depth=0 flat tree, ~1493 chars/page over 4 pages (50-60% of 2000-4000/page norm).
root_cause: Distinct from the cluster-level generic OCR-quality explanation: inspection of the actual 75 recovered blocks in processed/6025b212-36cd-4962-816c-cfe67c865110.flat.json shows all 8 Arabic article markers (المادة (1) through (8)) WERE recovered by OCR -- text loss is not the primary flatness cause here. The bug is a promotion-gate miss: 5/8 markers that appear as a bare, isolated line (blocks 6, 33, 58, 65, 68: e.g. 'المادة (6)') got promoted to role=title, but 3/8 markers that share a paragraph with the article's descriptive title text on one OCR line (blocks 43, 47, 49: e.g. 'المادة (3) نطاق التطبيق') stayed role=prose. _inject_arabic_structural_headings (src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:85-115) only promotes a line to a '## heading' when the prev_blank flag is True at converters.py:104 (the line must be preceded by a blank line in the raw Docling markdown). Docling's scanned-page OCR/layout engine fuses these 3 marker+title lines onto the same paragraph as adjacent body text without an intervening blank line, so the promotion at converters.py:109-112 never fires for them. Downstream, the flat block splitter's _FLAT_HEADING_RE check (src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py ~2287-2292) then classifies the un-prefixed line as ordinary prose instead of a title block, keeping the tree flat (depth=0) despite the article structure being textually present in the recovered OCR output.
code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:104 (_inject_arabic_structural_headings prev_blank gate, lines 85-115); src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py:~2287-2292 (_FLAT_HEADING_RE block-role classification)
suggested_fix: Loosen the Arabic structural-heading promotion condition so a line matching _AR_ARTICLE_RE/_AR_PART_RE at its START is split into its own heading + remaining prose text even when NOT preceded by a blank line (i.e. do not require prev_blank when the marker is a clean line-leading match), instead of requiring the whole line to be short AND paragraph-isolated. This recovers the marker+title-on-one-line pattern (المادة (N) <title>) that Docling scanned-page OCR frequently emits without paragraph breaks, alongside the already-working bare-marker case.

Pre-D2 (Run10), the pipeline kept 2 duplicate garbled-OCR blocks totaling 230 chars; D2's retry discards those in favor of the thinner post-OCR enrichment output, so content nets NEGATIVE for this specific document even though D2 was designed to rescue exactly this doc (named explicitly in the code comment at client.py:976-977).
